The loop-reasoning framework establishes a hierarchical causal structure where each layer (L0–L6) represents a distinct abstraction level of game dynamics. L0 encodes usage patterns, L1 captures health impacts, and L2 models matchups. These layers interact recursively: a change in usage (L0) necessitates recalibration of health (L1), which in turn affects matchup decisions (L2). This forms a closed-loop system where empirical feedback drives iterative refinement. Failure modes arise when layers are misaligned—such as reading L0 without validating L1 or publishing L2 before L1 is fully resolved. The system enforces correctness through traceability: all outputs must be verifiable against real-world inputs. The epistemic integrity of the model depends on ensuring that each layer's logic is grounded in observable data rather than speculative assumptions.
